citation.title: Topological dimensionality reduction-based machine learning for efficient gradient-free 3D topology optimization
citation.authors: Zhaoyou Sun; Yaguang Wang; Pai Liu; Yangjun Luo

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: The abstract claims that the DNN and material-field approach cuts computation time by roughly one to four orders of magnitude relative to coarse-mesh gradient-free optimization methods.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Abstract, p. 1 states 1–4 orders of magnitude, equivalent to 10–10,000×; numeric field records the lower bound, not a single measured factor. §4.1, p. 9 compares 1,941 FE calls with 4,000,000 GSA and 10,243 SOLO calls on different meshes.
claim.alternatives: §4.1, p. 9: 1,941 FE analyses versus 4,000,000 for GSA and 10,243 for SOLO; §4.2, pp. 11–12: 3D compliance 1.35% and 3.23% worse than gradient-based MFSE.

baseline.classical_method: coarse-mesh gradient-free methods, specifically generalized simulated annealing (GSA) and SOLO (§4.1, p. 9); gradient-based MFSE used for quality (§4.1–4.2)
baseline.problem_size: DNN-MFSE short cantilever: 80 × 80 elements; GSA/SOLO cited comparison: 11 × 11 elements (§4.1, p. 9); 3D cantilever: 48 × 16 × 6 and 96 × 32 × 12 elements (§4.2, pp. 11–12)
baseline.classical_iterations: GSA: 4 × 10^6 FE evaluations; SOLO: 10,243 FE evaluations (§4.1, p. 9)
baseline.training_time: not stated; DNN surrogate is trained within each optimization (§3, p. 8; §4.1, p. 9)
baseline.data_generation_cost: 1,941 FE evaluations for DNN-MFSE short cantilever (§4.1, p. 9); integrated in per-problem run
baseline.quality_metric: compliance in Nm (§4.1, Tables 2–3, pp. 10–11; §4.2, pp. 11–12), homogenized bulk modulus (§4.3), peak weld stress in MPa (§4.4)
baseline.quality_gap: 3D cantilever DNN-MFSE versus gradient MFSE: 4.41 versus 4.35 Nm and 3.80 versus 3.68 Nm (§4.2, pp. 11–12); short cantilever mean: 0.7564 versus 0.7472 Nm (Table 3, p. 11)

R1.evidence: Abstract, p. 1 and §4.1, p. 9: the speed claim compares FE counts with GSA/SOLO on 80 × 80 versus 11 × 11 meshes; no quality comparison with those speed baselines is given.

R2.evidence: Introduction, p. 2 calls existing density-based gradient-free methods inefficient; §4.1, p. 9 selects coarse-mesh GSA/SOLO as the speed baselines, with no solver or hardware information for a direct efficiency check.

R3.evidence: §3 and §4.1, pp. 8–9: the surrogate is trained by Latin-hypercube samples inside each optimization, so its FE calls belong to the per-problem run rather than an offline dataset.

R4.evidence: §4.1–4.4, pp. 9–16: returned designs have FE-based compliance, bulk-modulus or stress results; §4.3 states volume constraints are met, but no failed-design rate is reported.

reporting.n_test_cases: 5 problem families: 2D cantilever, 2D MBB, 3D cantilever, 2D/3D microstructures, dropped phone (§4, pp. 8–16); several volume variants

notes: The abstract states a wall-clock reduction, whereas §4.1 supports it with FE-evaluation counts cited from methods using a much coarser mesh. Section 4.1 reports ten random runs and Table 3 gives compliance variance.
